newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM to lobby G7 heads on Russia isles dispute.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM to lobby G7 heads on Russia isles dispute.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday he will press Russian President Boris Yeltsin to solve the two countries' territorial dispute at the upcoming Group of Seven (G7) summit.

"At my meeting with President Yeltsin, I intend to urge him to make utmost efforts to resolve the issue and secure a full-fledged peace," he told a news conference prior to his departure for Denver, Colorado.

Hashimoto said he would also seek support from U.S. President Bill Clinton and other fellow G7 leaders for Japan's stance on the half-century-old dispute, which has kept Tokyo and Moscow from signing a World War Two peace treaty.
Hashimoto told reporters Clinton assured him of U.S. support on the issue when the two discussed including Russia in the G7 summit.

The three days of talks starting on Friday have been formally dubbed the "Summit of the Eight," since Russia's Yeltsin will join the leaders of the G7 nations -- the United States, Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan.

Japan, whose strong initial resistance to Russia's joining G7 gatherings has given way to pragmatic acceptance of Moscow at the group's political talks, separates the territorial dispute from its bilateral economic relations with Russia.

But Hashimoto voiced scepticism that Russia had any place at G7 talks on financial and monetary issues and Japanese newspapers have quoted him as being cool toward moves at Denver to promote Moscow's membership in the World Trade Organisation.
The four Russian-controlled islands and islet groups, called the Northern Territories in Japan and the Southern Kuriles by Russia, were seized by the Soviet Union in the closing days of the war.
In a step toward regularising bilateral summits, Hashimoto was likely during his talks with Yeltsin to accept Moscow's invitation to visit Russia later this year, a foreign ministry official said.
